history.p: Already less than a month after the premiere of "Ravnen" (HartW 1) in October 1832, Hartmann started planning a new opera together with the poet Henrik Hertz, and in the middle of January 1833 they had a meeting with the director of The Royal Theatre. A few days later Hartmann received the text for the first scenes of "Corsarerne", the rest of act one followed a month later, and on Hartmann's birthday on 14 May Hertz finished his text. Hartmann end-dated his score 12 March 1835, and the premiere took place on 23 April. In 1883 Hartmann revised his music on the basis of a new version of Hertz's text which had been published in 1860, but this version was never performed. During his visit to Paris in 1839 Hartmann showed the score to Rossini, who was very positive but pointed out that there were too many different motifs.

physDesc.condition: Extremely worn with several loose pages.

physDesc.physMedium: Bound in cardboard cover with leather spine and corners and marbled sides. Handwritten label pasted on the front cover and inscribed: "297 / Corsarerne / Partitur / 1ste Act". Written in brown ink. Paper: 18 staves. Hartmann has paginated every bifolio only (1-61). In upper left and right-hand corner each number is paginated separately in foreign hand in pencil. At the bottom of the pages,paginated consecutively 1-300. German text added in pencil. No. 2 numerous emendations in purple ink, which has come off onto the back of the paper. On p. 1 of No. 5, Hartmann has written in pencil: "Characteren i dette Stykke vel ren forfeilet, da Oversætteren har antaget at denne Arie, som et Udtryk af Fortvivelse, skulde foredrages 'con molto fuoco'". Above No. 6 added in purple ink: "NB transp: til G dur." In this score the Romance is notated in D major. On p. 292 Hartmann has written in purple ink: "I Stedet for denne Slutning paa 1ste Akt benyttes det vedlagte efter Hertzs nye Udgave componerede Slutningsnumer." This attachment has been removed and is now to be found under the signature mu 8307.0491 MA ms 0432.

physDesc.physMedium: Bound in cardboard cover with leather spine and corners and marbled sides. Handwritten label pasted on the front cover and inscribed: "297 / Corsarerne / Partitur / 2den og 3die Act." Written in brown and black ink. Paper: 16 and 18 staves. Hartmann has continued his pagination of the bifolios (62-149), wheras the pagination at the bottom of the pages starts afresh with p. 1-367. No German text in this volume. No. 8 of the score has been changed to 8a, and 14 bars been replaced by a loose folio with six bars. On p. 15, a Cavatina ("Hvor jeg gaaer og hvor jeg dvæler er Hendes Billede mig nær") called 8 B has been marked "(indlagt) udelades" (to be omitted) in pencil in Hartmann's hand. The aria No. 10 ("Amor, du som lærte Qvinden at elske Manden saa ømt") has also been marked "udelades". On pp. 183-186 "Dands. Allegro" has been cancelled and marked "udgaaer" (to be omitted). On p. 223 from "vide §" to p. 227 § cancelled and marked "udgaaer") On pp. 297-302 "Allo: passionato, non troppo" marked "udgaaer". Apart from two bars on p. 299 "Larghetto". On p. 315 from "vide" to § on p. 318 cancelled. No. 14 Terzettino with reference to No. 15, Terzetto med Chor on p. 339. On p. 356 in Hartmann's hand: "NB I Stedet for det følgende No 16 see det nye vedlagte Slutningschor." (instead of the following No. 16 see the new appended final chorus.). At the end of the music on p. 371 signed and dated "I:P:E: Hartmann 12. Marts 1835".
Written in brown ink. Paper: 16 staves. At the top of p.1 Hartmann has written: "§ a tempo con fuoco sin al fine. Til No 2, Corsarerne 1ste Akt".

annot.p: A draft for the new ending of No. 2 from the beginning with the words "Det hele Slot til Grus forvandle", but only the first five bars have been orchestrated, the following eleven bars are vocal parts and the last three bars of vl.1. This ending was used on pp. 39-41 in the printed vocal score.

annot.p: On an un-numbered page after the title page: "'Korsarerne' opførtes første Gang paa det kongelige Theater den 23de April 1835. Af Musiken ere kun enkelte mindre Dele tidligere udkomne, medens Operaen først i denne Udgave fremtræder i sin Helhed. Ved denne Lejlighed har Komponisten foretaget en gjennemgaaende Revision af Musiken, og, af dramatiske og musikalske Hensyn, omarbejdet og forkortet den paa flere steder. De to første Akter slutte sig til Digterens senere Omarbejdelse af Stykket (H. Hertz's Dramatiske Værker XIV); i sidste Akt er derimod Scenegangen i Original-Udgaven fulgt". Beneath a short version of the plot of the opera.

I første Act af Stykket, som foregaaer i Italien, søger Huushovmesteren Tommaso at bagtale den unge Kjøbmand Diagoras, for hvem Gartnerens Datter Marietta har fattet Godhed. Marietta bliver fortørnet, og under Striden, som nu opstaaer, synges følgende Duet." Then the text of the duet follows, while the duet itself has been arranged by Hartmann for solo piano.
